title: sframe, instrument profile
description: The implemented profile: the shape surveyframe's write_sframe() emits as of 0.4.3. This is Layer 1 (instrument) of the five-layer model in sframe.schema.json, serialised flat rather than nested under `layers`, plus the verification hash. A file conforming to this profile is a complete, verifiable instrument declaration. It is not a complete provenance chain: response, analysis/reporting and manifest layers arrive with surveyframe 0.6.

cslNames.description: CSL names: {"family", "given"} for a person, {"literal"} for an organisation.

sframe_format.description: Version of the file format itself, distinct from the instrument's own `version` and from the package version. Consumers negotiate on this.

hash.description: SHA-256, hex-encoded, over the whole file with `hash.value` set to the empty string, serialised in the canonical form that `canonical` names. With `canonical` = "rfc8785" (surveyframe 0.4.3 and later) that form is RFC 8785, the JSON Canonicalization Scheme: object keys sorted by UTF-16 code units at every depth, numbers in their shortest round-trip form, strings minimally escaped, no whitespace, and the UTF-8 bytes of that text are hashed. `canonical` sits inside the hashed content, so changing it breaks the hash. A file without `canonical` was written before surveyframe 0.4.3, and its hash was taken with keys sorted in the writing session's locale order, or, before canonical serialisation, over jsonlite's default output in file order. Readers may check such a hash in those forms, and should ask for the file to be saved again. Reference implementations: sframe_hash_value() in surveyframe and sframeCanon() in its survey_builder.html.

canonical.description: The canonical form the hash was taken in. Optional so files written before surveyframe 0.4.3 still conform. A reader refuses any other value, since it cannot check a hash taken in a form it does not know.

version.description: The instrument's version, not the format's.

items.description: Declared items. `type` carries the measurement intent a consumer needs to pick a legitimate analysis.

ordered.description: Optional (surveyframe 0.4.3). True when the options run in a meaningful order, as in a frequency or an education scale, so a single_choice item on the set is ordinal. Present only when true, so a set without it hashes as it did before the field existed.

scales.description: Declared scales. A consumer reads these to know which items form a construct, which is what a bare CSV cannot express.

analysis_plan.description: Pre-declared analyses. Present here is what makes the file a pre-registration rather than a description.

objective.description: Optional (surveyframe 0.4.3). The id of the study objective this block serves, one of study.objectives[].id. An empty string names no objective. A block naming an objective the study does not declare is invalid, a check this schema cannot express and surveyframe's validate_sframe() makes.

hypotheses.description: Optional (surveyframe 0.4.3). The hypotheses the researcher declared before the data, printed by a report as written. A text null hypothesis, a text alternative, or both. SurveyBuilder writes null when none was written.

designs.description: Optional conjoint designs (surveyframe 0.4.0). Present only when the instrument declares at least one, so an instrument without them hashes as it did before the field existed.

amendments.description: Optional disclosed-revision log (surveyframe 0.4.0), appended by amend_sframe(). Present only when there is at least one entry. previous_hash and new_hash are SHA-256 content hashes over every top-level field except hash, amendments and references, taken in the same canonical form as `hash` (RFC 8785 from surveyframe 0.4.3, the locale-sorted form before it).

study.description: Optional (surveyframe 0.4.3). The study the instrument serves: the problem statement, the objectives, the sampling plan and the preregistration fields. Never shown to respondents, since telling them the aims can bias their answers. Inside the content hash and the amendment content hash, so a change to it after collection is a design amendment. Present only when something is declared, so an instrument without a study hashes as it did before this field existed. Objective ids are unique within the study, a check this schema cannot express and surveyframe's validate_sframe() makes.

problem.description: The problem statement, 1 short paragraph. surveyframe notes, without failing, a statement over 150 words.

id.description: Such as O1. A plan block names it in its objective field.

preregistration.description: Optional (surveyframe 0.4.3). What a preregistration asks for beyond the plan blocks, each a non-blank text, any of them absent. Inside the hash like the rest of the study, so a change after collection is a design amendment.

exclusion_rules.description: Which responses will be excluded, and why.

stopping_rule.description: When data collection ends: a date, a sample size or another rule.

primary_outcomes.description: The outcomes that answer the main question.

multiplicity.description: How the tests are corrected for being run together, if at all.

contingency.description: What will be done if an assumption fails or the planned sample is not reached.

method.description: Probability methods: simple_random, systematic, stratified, cluster. Non-probability methods: convenience, purposive, quota, snowball. census asks the whole population. other is described in method_other.

method_other.description: Describes an other method. Required, and not blank, when method is other, and absent otherwise.

references.description: Optional works the instrument cites (surveyframe 0.4.3), as CSL-JSON records: the format Zotero, Mendeley and pandoc share, so a host can hand them straight to a citation processor. Present only when the instrument has at least one, so an instrument that cites nothing hashes as it did before this field existed. Left out of the amendment content hash: citing a source is disclosure, and adding one to a published instrument needs no amendment.

id.description: Citation key, cited in text as [@id]. Unique within the instrument.

issued.description: CSL date: {"date-parts": [[year]]}, or {"literal": text} when the year is not a number.

container-title.description: The journal, or the book a chapter is in.

language.description: The work's language code, for example fr. A citation style title-cases English titles only.

cited_by.description: Where the instrument cites this work: "instrument", or "item:<id>", "scale:<id>", "plan:<block id>", "model:<id>", "hypothesis:<block id>" (the hypotheses that plan block declares) or "study". Each target must exist in the instrument: a hypothesis target names a block that declares a null or alternative hypothesis, and "study" needs a study. A reference with none is read as cited by the instrument as a whole. surveyframe drops this field when it hands the record to a citation processor.
